name: Geelong Waterfront
reason: Wikivoyage Geelong lists it as a working maritime area with cafes, carousel and gardens; open precinct, easily half an hour (rules 1-2).

name: Geelong Maritime Museum
reason: For: Wikivoyage Geelong lists a museum you go inside. Against: listing has no description, a single source, small museum (needs two counted sources).

name: Geelong Botanic Gardens
reason: Wikivoyage Geelong names the free botanical gardens (daily, tea house), a walkable half hour; second-tier city stop.

name: Torquay Surf Beach
reason: Back Beach is Torquay's surf beach; Wikivoyage Torquay region/Surf Coast plus greatoceanroad.com.au things-to-do and guides name it; surfing and sand walks (rule 1-2).

name: Point Addis
reason: Wikivoyage Johanna: surf beach with a 30-minute indigenous bushland walk to a lookout; named stop on the Surf Coast Walk.

name: Angahook-Lorne State Park
reason: Now part of Great Otway National Park; Wikivoyage mention is a generic walking-area line, not a distinct place; its draws (Lorne falls, walks) are separate spots (rule 3).

name: Marriner's Lookout
reason: For: Wikivoyage Apollo Bay lists a 30-minute return walk to a view over town and coast. Against: single source, short ordinary hill lookout above the town.

name: Blanket Bay
reason: Parks Victoria lists a Blanket Bay day visitor area and campground in Great Otway NP, a sheltered beach on the Great Ocean Walk; second-tier beach (rules 1-2).

name: Sheoak Falls
reason: Parks Victoria has a dedicated Sheoak Falls page near Lorne (600 m walk, with Swallow Cave option) plus Wikivoyage; waterfall walk of about an hour.

name: Lake Colac
reason: For: Wikivoyage Colac names the largest freshwater lake in Victoria, birdwatching, botanic gardens beside it. Against: one source, shallow drought-hit lake, plain town lakeshore.

name: Camperdown
reason: A town whose only listed draw on Wikivoyage is Mt Leura and the lakes view, which are the attractions; a town is not a spot beside its own attractions (COVERAGE: town wrapper).

name: Bay of Martyrs
reason: Wikivoyage Great Ocean Road only mentions it in passing beside Bay of Islands; a roadside viewing stop with no guide singling it out (rule 3).

name: The Crags
reason: Wikivoyage Port Fairy lists it as a popular scenic spot and sunset viewpoint 10 km away; second-tier coastal stop.

name: Port Fairy Museum and Archives
reason: Small local history museum in the old courthouse with one Wikivoyage listing; not a draw a visitor would go out of the way for (friend test).

name: East Beach, Port Fairy
reason: For: tourism board names it for whale watching, main town beach. Against: one source, overlaps Port Fairy's coast and Griffiths Island, no distinct activity beyond seasonal whales.

name: Warrnambool Art Gallery
reason: For: Wikivoyage Warrnambool lists a free gallery of about 5000 works with rotating exhibitions. Against: single source, regional council gallery, short visit.

name: Moyjil - Point Ritchie
reason: Wikivoyage Warrnambool describes the headland at the Hopkins mouth as a significant Aboriginal site with paths and southern right whale viewing in season.

name: Hopkins Falls
reason: Wikivoyage Warrnambool: 90 m wide falls 15 km out with picnic areas (eels migrate in summer); second-tier natural stop.

name: Lake Pertobe
reason: Wikivoyage Warrnambool lists the Lake Pertobe and foreshore parkland beside Flagstaff Hill; open all-day waterfront park.

name: Natural Bridge (Budj Bim)
reason: Wikivoyage Budj Bim describes it as part of the Lake Surprise attraction area of the park; part of a larger spot (rule 3).

name: Portland Maritime Discovery Centre
reason: For: Wikivoyage Portland lists a museum with a whale skeleton and visitor information. Against: single source, small regional museum.

name: Discovery Bay Coastal Park
reason: Parks Victoria park page: highest coastal cliffs in Victoria, Cape Nelson, Bridgewater seal colony walk, Lake Monibeong and beaches; a substantial park with named walks.
